scope: Read-only review of every assigned frozen title and complete ItemBody, plus every receipt-listed screenshot tile individually at original resolution. Reviewed for LaTeX/TikZ rendering defects, diagram mathematics, and source-supported high-likelihood missing diagram candidates.
coverage_label: Recovered body-preview coverage: titles and complete ItemBodies were reviewed from frozen snapshots and local preview tiles. This does not claim successful canonical parsing or native-loader coverage. The category has two strict YAML blockers recorded separately in frontmatter-parse-blockers.json; neither blocker is assigned to lane 03.

review_method.source_review: Frozen snapshot titles and complete ItemBodies inspected; current source and frozen snapshot SHA256 values compared to assignment.
review_method.rendering: Every receipt-listed tile opened individually with tools.view_image(detail="original"); no collage or downscale.
review_method.boundary: Read-only local repository review; no HTTP(S), live website, production or library source changes, builds, tests, or gates.

findings.title: Unwrapped TeX commands appear literally in prose

exact_text: where \odot and max are coordinatewise. Update
coordinatewise. Each coordinate of v_t and \widehat v^{\max}_t is nonnegative, and the denominator is at least epsilon>0, so every finite update is defined.

findings.evidence: The original-resolution tile visibly prints the literal backslash commands \odot and \widehat in prose instead of typeset inline mathematics. The surrounding update formulas render correctly. These are source text outside math delimiters, so the visible output is supported by the frozen source.
findings.repair_direction: Wrap the mathematical symbols in inline math delimiters or replace them with plain-language wording.

typography_observations.observation: An initial impression that the first F in each title was clipped was rejected after exact pixel crops of the standalone original tiles; the full FISTA and Fixed titles are visible at the left margin. No defect is recorded.

diagram_review.summary: Lane receipts report tikz_count 0 for all assigned items and no diagram failures. No existing rendered diagrams were available for diagram-mathematics checks.

source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.title: Newton, Cauchy, and truncated-CG steps on one indefinite model
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.rationale: The worked example directly compares an unrestricted Newton step outside the unit ball with feasible Cauchy/truncated-CG boundary steps and states their predicted reductions; a sketch can expose feasibility and direction relationships at a glance.
concrete_labels_and_relations_to_draw_or: Draw the unit trust-region circle centered at the origin.
Show the raw Newton point p_N=(−1,3)/√2 outside the circle and its line-search full-step role as stated.
Show the coincident feasible Cauchy and first truncated-CG boundary point p_C=(1,3)/√10 on the circle.
Label the indefinite quadratic model matrix B=diag(−1,1), gradient g=(−1,−3)/√2, and the stated predicted-reduction comparison; do not imply p_C equals p_N.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.classification: uncertain editorial candidate; no omission or mathematical defect is confirmed

source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.title: A finite-basis occupied projector map can two-cycle despite a uniform gap
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.rationale: The example’s central claim is the exact two-cycle P0↔P1 with gap 1 at both iterates; a compact state-transition diagram could make the counterexample immediate.
concrete_labels_and_relations_to_draw_or: Represent P0=diag(1,0) and P1=diag(0,1) as two nodes.
Draw Φ(P0)=P1 and Φ(P1)=P0 arrows; annotate gap 1 at each node.
Show the iteration P0,P1,P0,P1,… and mark ||P0−P1||_F=√2 to distinguish cycling from convergence.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.classification: uncertain editorial candidate; no omission or mathematical defect is confirmed

source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.title: The four McCormick inequalities give the convex hull of a bilinear graph over a box
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.rationale: The item identifies a three-dimensional graph and its convex hull via four McCormick planes; an optional view can connect the inequalities to the geometric envelope.
concrete_labels_and_relations_to_draw_or: Show two lower and two upper affine McCormick planes and their intersection polytope enclosing the graph.
For normalized coordinates, mark graph vertices (0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(1,1,1), matching the convex-combination proof.
If degenerate box widths are illustrated, show the envelope collapsing to the product graph as stated in lines 50–54.
